;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Saudi Arabian-led intervention in Yemen]], [[Yemeni Civil War (2015–present)]]
**The [[Cabinet of Yemen#Current_cabinet|Yemeni Ministry of Defense]] says 300 people were killed and wounded in [[United Arab Emirates]] air raids in southern [[Yemen]] over the two previous days. The [[Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation (United Arab Emirates)|UAE Foreign Ministry]] has said the "preemptive operation" targeted "terrorist militias". [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2019/08/uae-targets-terrorist-militias-fractures-saudi-grow-190830080042582.html (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Israel–Lebanon conflict]]
**[[Israeli Defense Forces]] name three senior [[Iran]]ian officers and point out that the leader of the [[Quds Force]] is in Lebanon "with his family". Amid the campaign for the 17 September [[September 2019 Israeli legislative election|legislative election]], Israel says Iran is moving to convert [[Hezbollah]]'s arsenal of what Israel says is more than 100,000 rockets into precision-guided missiles. [https://amp.cnn.com/cnn/2019/08/30/middleeast/israel-lebanon-tensions-intl/index.html (CNN)]

;International relations
*[[Pope Francis]] sends a video message to the people of [[Mozambique]] before his visit to the African country next week. He stresses reconciliation after years of conflict.  The Pontiff says that “although I will be unable to travel beyond the capital, my heart reaches out and embraces you all, with a special place for those who live in difficulty.” [https://press.vatican.va/content/salastampa/en/bollettino/pubblico/2019/08/30/190830a.html (Holy See Press Office)]

;Law and crime
*[[Brexit]]
**A [[Court of Session]] judge refuses to grant an interdict, the [[Scots law|Scottish equivalent]] to an injunction, preventing the upcoming suspension of the [[Parliament of the United Kingdom|UK Parliament]]. The judge rules there is "no cogent need" for such an emergency measure as the suspension is not scheduled until September 9. However, a full hearing on the lawfulness of the suspension is brought forward to Tuesday. The case against the UK government is being brought by [[Member of the Scottish Parliament|Members]] of the [[Scottish Parliament]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-scotland-scotland-politics-49521132 (BBC News)]
**Former [[Prime Minister of the United Kingdom|Prime Minister]] Sir [[John Major]] announces he will join a case brought by anti-Brexit campaigner [[Gina Miller]] seeking [[judicial review]] of Parliament's suspension in the [[High Court of Justice|High Court]] under [[English law]]. The case challenges the lawfulness of current UK Prime Minister [[Boris Johnson]]'s advice to [[Elizabeth II|Queen Elizabeth II]] in asking her to suspend the UK Parliament. The case is due for a preliminary hearing next Thursday with a full hearing the following day if the High Court approves one. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-politics-49523055 (BBC News)]
**The [[Courts of Northern Ireland#High Court|High Court]] in [[Belfast]] hears a claim under [[Northern Ireland law|Northern Irish law]] brought by [[Raymond McCord]], a campaigner for [[The Troubles|Troubles]] victims, challenging the constitutionality of suspending the UK Parliament. Sir [[Declan Morgan]], The [[Lord Chief Justice of Northern Ireland]], adjourns proceedings until next week. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-northern-ireland-49522042 (BBC News)]
**A cross-party group of over fifty members of the suspended Parliament pledge to carry on meeting in the absence of Parliament. [https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2019/aug/30/more-than-50-rebel-mps-pledge-to-convene-alternative-parliament (''The Guardian'')]
*[[2019 Hong Kong anti-extradition bill protests|Hong Kong protests]]
**Prominent [[Hong Kong]] [[pro-democracy camp (Hong Kong)|pro-democracy]] activists [[Joshua Wong]] and [[Agnes Chow]] are arrested, charged and released on bail. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-asia-china-49520025 (BBC News)]
*[[September 11 attacks]]
**A [[Guantanamo military commission|military judge]] sets 11 January 2021 as the starting date for the selection of a [[United States military jury|military jury]] in the [[United States v. Khalid Sheikh Mohammed|trial of five suspects]], among which is [[Khalid Sheikh Mohammed]], held in [[Guantanamo Bay detention camp|Guantanamo Bay]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2019/aug/30/khalid-shaikh-mohammad-9-11-trial-start-date (''The Guardian'')]
*[[List of mass shootings in the United States in 2019]]
**At least 10 teenagers (age 15 to 18) are injured in a mass shooting at a high school football game at [[Ladd–Peebles Stadium]] in [[Mobile, Alabama]]. [https://www.cnn.com/2019/08/31/us/mobile-ladd-peebles-stadium-shooting/index.html (CNN)]
;Politics and elections
*[[Politics of the United States]]
**[[Madeleine Westerhout]] is forced to resign as Director of [[Oval Office Operations]] at the [[White House]] after leaking private information about the [[Trump family]] and White House operations to reporters at a private dinner. Westerhout had allegedly bragged about her personal access to [[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Donald Trump]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-us-canada-49527707 (BBC News)]
**White House aides admit that President Trump made up a phone call from China last weekend. [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/americas/us-politics/trump-china-phone-call-lie-fact-check-g7-summit-trade-war-a9085786.html (''The Independent'')]
